📡 National cohesion in Pezeshkian Administration; an asset for overcoming crises

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Over the past two years, President Masoud Pezeshkian's administration, despite various crises and challenges, has strived to bring the government and society closer together and transcend political binaries, thereby paving the way for the formation and strengthening of national cohesion.

The results of this strategy become evident during pivotal moments, when, regardless of their divergent perspectives, people have rallied together in defense of national interests and the safeguarding of Iran.
​
In the eyes of the Pezeshkian administration, this national solidarity is not merely a societal milestone, it is a powerful asset that enables the nation to overcome any challenge.
​
The 14th administration began its work at a time when Iranian society was grappling with a host of accumulated issues.
​
Under such circumstances, national cohesion was not merely a political concept for the Pezeshkian administration; it gradually became one of the essential requirements for steering the country through crisis.
​
The significance of this issue grew even more when the country faced security crises and war.
​
The 12-day war and the subsequent 40-day war placed Iranian society in a position where many disagreements and differences were set aside in the face of a greater concern, preserving Iran and overcoming an external threat.
​
Pezeshkian later described the 12-day war as a symbol of Iranian national unity and stated that the people of Iran, regardless of their personal preferences and views, acted as one when defending their country.
​
He further stressed that the nation’s lasting strength resides in the unity of its people, the potential of its young generation, and optimism for what lies ahead.
​
It is important to note that national unity does not require everyone to think alike. A society of millions, with its broad spectrum of political, cultural, social, and economic perspectives, will inevitably hold differing views.
​
However, the crucial point is that at decisive junctures, these divergences do not obstruct the emergence of common interests.
​
In the recent security crises, this reality proved to be among the most significant. While citizens may have held grievances regarding various domestic matters, policies, and official conduct, a challenge to the nation’s territorial sovereignty was an entirely distinct and overriding concern.
​
This is exactly what distinguishes authentic national cohesion from empty political rhetoric.
​
True unity emerges when people, even in the absence of full consensus on every issue, recognize a common fate in matters of existential importance.
​
Pezeshkian, in his own account of the war, has similarly emphasized the role of the people.
​
After the 40-day war ended, he described the conscious presence of the people as a factor in neutralizing destabilizing scenarios and strengthening national cohesion, adding that this popular presence is an asset that must be utilized in the country’s reconstruction and progress.
​
This perspective carries an important message: the people are not merely recipients of government policies; in times of crisis, they themselves are part of the solution.
​
While the war served as the ultimate test of national unity, the notion of cohesion extends far beyond the battlefield. A society genuinely coheres when it is capable of navigating not only external threats but also economic strain, resource shortages, service interruptions, and the ordinary anxieties of daily life. From this perspective, ensuring the continuity of everyday existence during crises is an essential component of sustain . . .
